rationale: no specific curve family was indicated, so the primary X25519 + ML-KEM-768 profile is recommended as the default hybrid
the current certificate uses RSA-2048; moving to ECDSA-P256 reduces handshake size, which partly offsets the larger post-quantum key share
harvest-now-decrypt-later exposure is 'high', so classical fallback is disallowed: a connection that falls back is exactly the one an attacker would record
the asset currently permits TLS1.2; every pqtls-lab profile is TLS 1.3 only, so TLS 1.2 clients will need to be identified first
caveats: This recommendation changes KEY ESTABLISHMENT only. Authentication stays classical, so the asset is protected against harvest-now-decrypt-later but is NOT protected against an adversary with a quantum computer who is able to forge signatures at connection time.

With fallback disabled, clients that do not support the hybrid group will FAIL to connect rather than downgrade. Run the legacy-client-compatibility test and plan the client rollout before enforcing this.
ML-DSA-65 is listed as the experimental authentication target only. It is capability-gated in pqtls-lab, has no public CA support, and must not be treated as a deployment option.
